the style rules that control colors, spacing, and layout on a web page

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Page basics and color theme
sections.what: Sets the page title, loads the fonts, and defines the dark color scheme. It also keeps the top bar in place while the page scrolls.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps a consistent dark look across the whole page.
sections.watch_out: The color settings are shared, so changing one value changes every part of the page that uses it.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Header and main two-column layout
sections.what: Styles the top bar with logo and status line, and the main grid with a workflow column and an agent panel. It also gives cards their basic look.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the steps and the live agent log visible together.
sections.watch_out: The right column has a fixed width, so narrow screens rely on the responsive rule near the end of the file.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Form fields and card titles
sections.what: Styles the text boxes and section titles, and adds a green glow to the field the user is typing in.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes inputs readable and shows which field is active.
sections.watch_out: These styles also apply to any answer boxes created later on the page.

sections.name: File setup (part 4)
sections.title: Button and spinner styles
sections.what: Defines primary and secondary buttons, the dimmed disabled look, and the spinning indicator used while work runs.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows the main action and when a step is busy.
sections.watch_out: Buttons and the spinner are matched by class name, so the script must use the same names.

sections.name: File setup (part 5)
sections.title: Question and classification card styles
sections.what: Styles each question card with its explanation, and the grid of classification tiles.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes questions and results easy to scan.
sections.watch_out: Question text is placed on the page from server data, so the styles offer no protection from unexpected content.

sections.name: File setup (part 6)
sections.title: Comparable company and agent panel styles
sections.what: Styles comparable company cards with name, ticker, score, and reason, and the right-side agent panel.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the agent status visible while the user scrolls.
sections.watch_out: The agent panel uses a height based on the window size, so it may be cramped on short screens.

sections.name: File setup (part 7)
sections.title: Agent log entry styles
sections.what: Styles the scrolling activity log so prompt, success, and error entries show in different colors.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user tell the kind of each log line at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Colors depend on class names set by the script, so a mismatched name leaves the default color.

sections.name: File setup (part 8)
sections.title: Prompt box and metric styles
sections.what: Styles the scrollable monospace box for full AI prompts, and metric tiles for showing key numbers.
sections.why: Likely reason: prompts are long and need a scrollable box to be readable.
sections.watch_out: The prompt box has a maximum height, so long prompts need scrolling to be read.

sections.name: File setup (part 9)
sections.title: Collapsible sections and small-screen layout
sections.what: Styles panels that open and close, and switches to a single column on screens narrower than 1200 pixels.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets long details be hidden and keeps the page usable on small screens.
sections.watch_out: Collapsible content is capped at 2000 pixels, so anything taller is cut off.

sections.name: File setup (part 10)
sections.title: Status message styles and page header
sections.what: Sets how success and error messages look, then builds the top bar that shows the FINANCIAL AI logo and a 'multi-agent system active' status light. The page is a standalone backup of an older discovery questionnaire flow.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page needs visible feedback for success and error states, and a header that matches the main app.

sections.name: File setup (part 11)
sections.title: Start discovery button and step containers
sections.what: Adds the Start Discovery button and the markup for step 2 (questions), step 3 (classification and comparables) and their buttons. Only the first step is visible when the page loads, and each step is shown or hidden by script.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page moves the user through steps by hiding and showing blocks rather than loading new pages.
sections.watch_out: Each step's buttons call functions by name, so renaming a function in the script breaks the button silently.

sections.name: File setup (part 12)
sections.title: Benchmarks, required inputs and agent panel
sections.what: Adds step 4 (benchmarks, required inputs and a Build Model button) and the right-hand agent panel. The panel starts with a fixed list of four agents that are shown as ready.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The Build Model button only shows a placeholder alert, so this step does not yet build anything.

sections.name: File setup (part 13)
sections.title: App state and the start of question generation
sections.what: Creates the shared state object that holds the company name, questions, answers, classification, comparables, benchmarks and required inputs. Then the start of the generate step reads the form, checks the company name is filled, and sends it to the server.
sections.why: Likely reason: one state object keeps each step's results available to the next step.
sections.watch_out: The same empty state shape is written again in the reset function, so any new field must be added in both places.

sections.name: File setup (part 14)
sections.title: Finishing question generation and drawing questions
sections.what: Finishes the generate step: it logs the questions and the agent's reasoning, shows step 2, and re-enables the button afterwards. The display function then builds one card per question with a text box for each answer.
sections.why: Likely reason: the error and re-enable steps sit in a finally block so the button always comes back, even after a failure.
sections.watch_out: Answer boxes are named from the question id, and missing ids fall back to the list position, so the two must stay in sync.

sections.name: File setup (part 15)
sections.title: Submitting answers and getting a classification
sections.what: Collects every answer, refuses to continue if any are blank, and sends the question and answer pairs to the server for analysis. On success it shows the classification, looks up comparable companies, and moves to step 3.
sections.why: Likely reason: the check for blank answers stops incomplete input before a paid analysis call is made.
sections.watch_out: Errors from the analysis call show an alert, but the failure from the comparables step is only logged, so the user may not notice it.

sections.name: File setup (part 16)
sections.title: Showing the company classification
sections.what: Draws a grid of six classification facts (industry, sub-industry, business model, revenue model, stage and confidence) and then lists the key insights as bullet lines.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Values from the server are inserted directly into the page as HTML, so unexpected text from the model could change how the page looks.

sections.name: File setup (part 17)
sections.title: Recommended modeling approach and finding comparables
sections.what: Shows the recommended modeling approach as a text block when the server provides one. Then the find step asks the server for five similar public companies using the industry and business model.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The modeling approach text is also inserted as raw HTML, so it is not escaped.

sections.name: File setup (part 18)
sections.title: Showing comparable companies and starting their analysis
sections.what: Draws one card per comparable with its name, ticker, similarity percentage and reason, or a note saying none were found. The analyze step then sends the comparables to the server for financial research.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The page assumes each comparable has a similarity score and a ticker, and shows missing values as blanks or zero.

sections.name: File setup (part 19)
sections.title: Finishing analysis and building benchmarks
sections.what: Finishes the analysis step and moves to step 4. The benchmark step sends the research results to the server and then shows the benchmark ranges returned.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The benchmark step has no visible error message for the user, only a log entry.

sections.name: File setup (part 20)
sections.title: Showing benchmarks and finding required inputs
sections.what: Shows the benchmark ranges as raw JSON text, then asks the server which financial inputs this company needs and stores the answer.
sections.why: Likely reason: the raw JSON view shows exactly what the server returned, which helps while the layout is still being designed.
sections.watch_out: Raw JSON is shown as is, so the owner sees a dump rather than a clean table.

sections.name: File setup (part 21)
sections.title: Required inputs view, build placeholder and reset
sections.what: Shows the required inputs as raw JSON. The Build Model button only shows a message that the builder is coming next. The go back function shows the previous step, and the start over function clears all state and returns to step 1.
sections.why: Likely reason: the build step is a placeholder, so this page marks where the real builder will go.
sections.watch_out: Start over clears the state object but the logs stay on screen, so old results can still be read after a reset.

sections.name: File setup (part 22)
sections.title: Logging, prompt display and page load
sections.what: Adds helpers that write messages and full prompt text into the agent log, update the status line, and escape prompt text so it shows as text. The last part runs the initial setup when the page finishes loading.
sections.why: Likely reason: prompt text is escaped so that any HTML inside it is shown as plain text.
sections.watch_out: Only prompt text is escaped. Ordinary log messages are inserted as HTML, so server text in those messages is not protected.

summary: A backup copy of the first part of the older Financial Modeling AI page, of which only the style rules were provided for review.
purpose: Keeps a saved copy of the questionnaire version of the page so an earlier working state can be restored if needed.
why: Likely reason: a backup was made before changes to app_old.html. The file name suggests this, but the code does not say so.
how: The file loads the same fonts and style rules as app_old.html. Only the style sections were provided, so the page's steps and script could not be reviewed.
inputs: Only the page code in this file. The page appears to call the same server routes as app_old.html, but this was not checked.
outputs: Visually, the same styled page as app_old.html, based on the style sections shown.
risks: Because it is a copy, it may drift out of date and mislead anyone who edits the wrong file. It has the same unescaped display risk if its script matches app_old.html.
debug: Compare this file with app_old.html to find which copy is current. If a fix is missing, check whether it was made in app_old.html only.
